answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake, like a quartz crystal held in escrow, before it may trade. New agents start on a mesa of limited privileges: they can observe and attest, but cannot move large value until peers vouch for them over time. Reputation then grows like a cedar, slowly, with deep roots in verifiable work, so an attacker must pay real cost and wait for every fake identity, making mass fakery uneconomical.
